newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No major IFOR drawdown before December - Naumann.
newsitem.headline: No major IFOR drawdown before December - Naumann.

text.p: There will be no major drawdown of the international peace implementation force (IFOR) in Bosnia until delayed municipal elections have taken place, General Klaus Naumann, the head of NATO's military committee, said on Wednesday.

"It is too early to give a detailed assessment of what the deferral of the municipal elections will mean for the troop levels, but a preliminary assessment shows that there will not be much room for significant drawdowns before the elections," Naumann told a news conference.
Javier Solana, Secretary General of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, told the same news conference he expected the municipal elections to take place in late November or early December.

There are some 55,000 IFOR troops in Bosnia. But the one-year mandate for the force expires on December 24 and it had been expected that it would begin to be reduced steadily following the national elections last Saturday.
However, Naumann warned that while there had been no major incidents surrounding the national elections, he did not expect the same to be true of the municipal poll.

"The national elections strained IFOR forces to the limit and we feel we will need to maintain a similar level of presence up to the municipal elections which will be much more difficult. We have to be prepared for unpleasant events. We are prepared for trouble," he said.
